items.content_html:
Over time, it is expected that the setups for Lix and Nix will diverge in some ways. To prevent cluttering the modules too much, we will introduce a separate Lix module. It begins its existence as a fork of the nix-daemon module, right now without major changes, although this will change soon. It is also slightly weird due to not having any option definitions on its own and instead dispatching on the pname of nix.package, which is done for backwards compatibility (particularly on 25.11), and will also change soon by the gradual introduction of a separate programs.lix option subtree.

Module and package were unmaintained, crusty, and the package cannot be built with modern npm tooling because of some jank in its lockfile that I cannot even begin to understand. I do not feel that this package is a good fit for nixpkgs considering the massive lockfile patch that would need to be vendored to support it, nor do I think that node2nix-generated package sets are any better(Hell, they're worse, since they add eval time)

Moved the line setting EDITOR to nano out of nixos/environment into nixos/nano so that it is only set when it's available on the system. Tried to stay consistent with nixos/vim.
nano.defaultEditor defaults to nano.enable instead of true so that there won't be an error in current configs if nano.enable is false while still throwing an error if the former is explicitly set to true while the latter to false.

items.content_html:
This PR is effectively a rewrite of the entire oidentd nixos module.

Some highlighted changes are:

  • Socket activated units.
  • Settings options for multiple config files.
  • Options for setting extra flags.
  • Systemd hardening.
  • Reloadable units.
  • Firewall options.
  • Allow listening on different addresses.
  • Removal of the fixed uid/gid oidentd user/group
  • Added NixOS test
  • Add h7x4 to maintainer lists for both package, module and test.
